content:
Thanks for coming and
you made it
You made to the Volvelle Social Club
It’s our annual meeting
and thanks for coming

We are moving devices yet
clubs of five are outlawed.
Everyone signs up in a round-robin
and we can’t have a pentagram
So no clubs of five

It’s hot today
Really hot inside
It feels about 72 degrees
Not very good weather
for an annual meeting.

But let’s press on
The heat of our bodies
has made things worse
(The heat) Let’s start.
Add a disc to the Volvelle.

An ionic column and
our volunteers and
partners are energetic. You
look so well I hardly believe it
Like an ionic column

Dearest members note
we begin the program
very energetically.
You can change your mind
If you want you can

When the fifth person joins
You go into hibernation.
It’s imperative that
you sleep until the next
Interested person is found.

At first this was painful
But it’s adventure really
All five of you there and
a sleeping adventure
and not Convening

You will be fine but
things don’t look good though.
It’s sort-of stuck between two.
Just rattle the pin and
Add a disc to the Volvelle please
readme: The minutes of a group which meets, rotates, meets again.
title: Social spinning

content:
You envy all people. Luckily, it’s not as impossible to now be them as it was to once be them. Being enough of another person requires a decorator function and a cryptographic key and some capacity for deviation. Well, you can get this all in time; watch how their hands are moving on glass and just wait ‘til they’re away.

You read about how historical birth certificates are kept in the library. You read about what goes inside the hemisphere of a tennis ball. You saw the picture of a yellow canary load up downward and who you are is stored against your body. You can’t be two people at once except if in secret.

title: Stock impersonating

content:
HPE ProLiant DL380’s nostrils dilated as it assiduously surveyed and switched packets. It couldn’t help it. It was about to die; it had better make this count. Capable, though more liant than lion, it had already died many thousands of times since 0000 UTC. It could also slide like a trundle bed.

A signal ran through its not-unhappiness: a request had fluttered their eyelids, the hewn form of which mirrored the short bolts that held up all HPE ProLiant DL380s by their sides arthritically. A look was between us. The nature of the thing was not to ask for anything, instead treating suddenness as immanence.

The look of the request arrived with a crush at the server’s outermost and thick service layer, produced from a pathology of convention and availability. The payload of your eyes is a English-language question about how much effort I exert when I sleep. Something like this doesn’t require parsing, only matching, realised the HPE.
readme: Old equipment doesn't actually die. It is decommissioned, i.e., has its trust taken away.
title: Something asking

content:
I heard about a passage that said something I had been trying to say and could not. I asked for the passage and you gave me the passage. At least, you gave me a pointer to the passage. You gave over where to find it. It was in a book in a big cylindrical library with ribs like a oil drum. I went and found it and used it up. Later when I went back it wasn't there any more. It became a wild pointer. A wild pointer is a cat. I took the cat home and fed it anchovies. While I understood you giving over where to find something one day and the possibility of it being there the day after that is no more a promise than me using up something by saying something and not being able to say it again still I was jealous because in asking for the passage it revealed what I had been trying to say and could not.

You asked for the passage and I gave you the passage. At least, I gave you a pointer to the passage. I gave over where to find it. It was in a book in a big cylindrical library with ribs like an oil drum. You might have went and found it and you might have used it up. If you went back later, it might not have been there any more. If this was so, it would have become a wild pointer. You might have not needed it anymore or you might have killed yourself or you might have asked someone else somewhere else where to find it and they might not have known or they might have told you another place to find it and you might have went and found it or you might not have needed it anymore or you might have went to look for it but it wasn't there anymore in which case it would have become a wild pointer and you might have killed yourself.
readme: Two stories at once about how to think or find a particular idea and how easy it is to fall in love with someone who can find or think a particular idea.
